task: Tendon adaptation to mechanical loading & tendinopathy -- the LOAD-ADAPTATION/remodeling layer + the tendinopathy dysfunction pole, distinct from the twin's existing tendon-elastic/strain/slack certs (the passive mechanical-spring baseline this layer adapts). Model: (a) load->stiffness/CSA dose-response, (b) overload->tendinopathy transition (load-tolerance envelope), (c) eccentric/HSR rehab efficacy. Two symmetric falsifiers: (1) a 'tendon is a passive inert spring, no biological adaptation' adversary must FAIL to reproduce measured training-induced stiffening; (2) an 'inflammatory (tendinitis)' adversary must MISPREDICT relative to a 'degenerative (tendinosis)' model on treatment response (anti-inflammatories) while the degenerative model correctly predicts failed-healing + eccentric-rehab efficacy.
confidence_tier: HIGH for the core dose-response/threshold/histology/RCT numbers (13 PMIDs, every one indepedently live-verified this session via NCBI eutils esearch+esummary+efetch, verbatim abstract text extracted, not recalled/trusted from the two pre-existing agent_outputs files this session found and built on). MEDIUM for the Cook & Purdam 3-stage terminology (reactive/dysrepair/degenerative) -- the continuum CONCEPT is directly confirmed live from the primary 2009 abstract + its own 2016 follow-up, but the literal 3-stage names are a widely-cited secondary characterization, not verbatim-quoted from a fetched full-text this session (abstracts only). LOW/inherited (not independently re-verified this session, carried from pre-existing repo agent_outputs with that caveat disclosed): sex/age modifiers (Onambele-Pearson 2012, McMahon 2018, Reeves 2003), AAS mismatch mechanism, nutrient-timing levers -- out of this task's explicit scope, mentioned only as pointers.

model.load_dose_response: Per-bout stimulus S(eps_peak): a THRESHOLD-GATED function of peak cyclic tendon strain, not of repetition count, frequency, or contraction mode. S=0 for eps_peak < eps_th; S rises toward 1 between eps_th and eps_sat. eps_th ~3% is a MODELING INTERPOLATION (not itself directly measured) bracketed by Arampatzis 2007's own measured null point (2.85%, no adaptation) and positive point (4.55%, adaptation) -- disclosed as an interpolation, not a swept threshold. eps_sat ~6.5% is Bohm 2014's own highest cleanly-significant tested magnitude (the 'reference protocol'), not asserted as a hard ceiling -- no adaptation-training study in this evidence base tested the 6.5-8% range, an honest gap. S is explicitly NOT a function of contraction type (isometric/concentric-eccentric/eccentric: Bohm 2015 SMD not significantly different; Beyer 2015 ECC vs HSR not significantly different in a diseased population) and only weakly of frequency/duration relative to magnitude (Bohm 2015: frequency not a significant moderator; Bohm 2014: high strain RATE alone gave only a non-significant tendency, P=0.08-0.09, vs magnitude+duration's clean P<0.05).
model.rate_mismatch: Three decorrelated state variables driven by the same leaky-integrated suprathreshold stimulus history S_bar(t), each with its OWN empirically-distinct time constant (within the SAME n=8 cohort, Kubo 2010): strength/neural activation (tau_strength, fast -- significant by month 2: +29.6%/+7.3%) vs muscle CSA + tendon stiffness (tau_tendon, slow -- not significant until month 3: +40.5%/+8.9% and stiffness/CSA sig only at the 3-month mark). Bohm 2015's own cross-study duration subgroup (>=12wk marginally, non-significantly, beats 8-12wk) is consistent with, not a duplicate re-derivation of, this single-cohort finding. During any period where demand (tracking the FAST strength channel) is deliberately ramped, tendon capacity (rate-limited by the SLOW channel) structurally cannot keep pace -- a geometric consequence of the two time constants, not an assumed injury mechanism.
model.load_tolerance_envelope: Define capacity C(t) proportional to k(t)*CSA(t) (the tendon's own current mechanical state from the dose-response channel) and demand D(t) (the mechanical loading actually imposed, which under progressive-overload training tracks the FAST strength channel). The dimensionless ratio R(t)=D(t)/C(t) is the governing scalar: R<=1 sustained -> homeostatic remodeling (the normal operating loop of the dose-response model above); R>1 transient/acute -> Cook & Purdam's proposed 'reactive tendinopathy' regime (acute, proliferative, reported clinically reversible with load management -- matches their own abstract's 'neither degenerative nor failed-healing alone explains presentation' framing for this early stage); R>>1 SUSTAINED (because dD/dt structurally outpaces dC/dt during aggressive progression, per the rate-mismatch above) -> progression toward 'tendon dysrepair' then 'degenerative tendinopathy', matching the ACTUAL histology (Khan 1999, Astrom & Rausing 1995: disorganized collagen, mucoid ground substance, neovascularization, ABSENT inflammatory cells). The key point is geometric, not a single absolute-load threshold: it is the RATE mismatch between a fast-rising demand and a slow-rising capacity that defines the danger zone, not any fixed Newton or percent-MVC number in isolation.
model.tendinosis_not_tendinitis: The dysfunction pole is modeled as a DEGENERATIVE (tendinosis), not inflammatory (tendinitis), process: histology at high R(t) shows disorganized collagen + mucoid ground substance + neovascularization + ABSENCE of inflammatory cells (Khan 1999 review; Astrom & Rausing 1995 primary n=163: 90% of symptomatic vs 20% of asymptomatic biopsies). This makes a DIFFERENT, checkable prediction than an inflammatory model: anti-inflammatory treatment should not resolve the underlying pathology. Falsifier forced to its strongest fair form (a double-blind placebo-RCT assaying gene expression directly, Heinemeier 2017, n=26): ibuprofen produced NO change in collagen-I/III or TGF-beta gene expression, NO change in VISA-A/pain/tendon-thickness -- the inflammatory model's own directly-testable prediction fails. Andres & Murrell 2008 review and Alfredson 1998's 100%-failure conventional-treatment arm (which explicitly included NSAIDs) corroborate at the clinical-outcome level across two independent, decorrelated methodologies (molecular RCT vs clinical-outcome comparison, 19 years apart).
model.rehab_efficacy: Eccentric loading (Alfredson) / heavy-slow-resistance (HSR, Beyer) rehab is modeled as a controlled, progressive re-application of the SAME dose-response stimulus S(eps_peak) to a tendon currently in the dysrepair/degenerative regime -- deliberately bringing R(t) back toward ~1 (controlled reloading) rather than either of the two failure modes: uncontrolled overload (R>>1, the original injury mechanism) or complete rest (S(eps)=0 indefinitely, which per this same dose-response curve drives NO remodeling stimulus at all and, per Alfredson 1998's own conventional-treatment arm which included rest, empirically failed 15/15 times). This is a single, economical, testable unification -- one dose-response function explains both healthy adaptation and rehabilitation, not two separate ad hoc mechanisms. The 'eccentric contraction is uniquely required' adversary was forced via Bohm 2015 (healthy population, contraction-type SMD not significantly different) AND Beyer 2015 (diseased population RCT, n=58, ECC vs HSR: 'none of these robust clinical and structural improvements differed between groups') -- it falls in BOTH, a genuinely diverse instance-space (different populations, decades, research groups, and health states).

distinct_from_existing_graph_node.why_distinct: The existing MECHANISM_TENDON_ELASTIC/STRAIN/SLACK_SENSITIVITY docs model the tendon as a FIXED (single-gait-cycle, non-adapting) elastic element; this document adds the TIME-VARYING remodeling layer (weeks-to-months state variables) plus the entire dysfunction/pathology pole (histology, continuum, rehab RCTs), neither of which existed in any prior doc.

honest_gaps: eps_th (~3%) and eps_sat (~6.5%) are MODELING INTERPOLATIONS between a small number of discrete measured points (2.85% null, 4.55% positive, 6.5% highest-tested-positive) -- no study in this evidence base swept a continuous strain-magnitude dose-response curve; precision beyond 'somewhere between 2.85% and 4.55%' / 'at least up to 6.5%, untested above that up to the ~8-9.9% failure-strain range already anchored in the sibling MECHANISM_TENDON_STRAIN.md doc' should not be over-read.

No single cohort in this evidence base tracked stiffness + CSA + a synthesis-marker (PICP/FSR) + strength together across one continuous multi-month time course; the tau_tendon >> tau_strength ordering is well-supported (Kubo 2010 within-cohort) but the mechanistic collagen-synthesis-marker time-course that would fully close the causal chain is a cross-study synthesis in the pre-existing agent_outputs file, not a single decisive dataset -- carried forward as an inherited, disclosed gap, not newly resolved this session.
